## Networking and multiplayer

### Type-6 participant-input frame construction (`004c60c0`, `004c6870`, `004c61e0`)

`SubmitNetworkPlayerInput` is the sole caller of `BuildNetworkInputFrameWithFallback` in the current Ghidra xrefs. In transport mode 1 with the host-role flag set, it enters the race synchronization critical section, appends the local four-byte input sample, and returns if that append fails. If the local-only state flag `006fd50c` is clear, it builds the frame, leaves the critical section, and sends `0x21` (33) bytes from a stack buffer. The first byte is message type 6; the remaining 32 bytes are the frame area. This fixed send length is explicit at `004c6140..004c6146`.

The builder derives a ring index from participant row zero's producer sequence minus one, masked to 127, then iterates the configured-human count. For each row whose ready flag is clear, it increments that row's producer sequence, marks the slot ready, copies the preceding four-byte sample (wrapping slot zero to slot 127), and applies `AND 0x8d` to byte `+3`. Thus bits 0, 2, 3 and 7 are retained and bits 1, 4, 5 and 6 cleared only in this synthesized missing-sample path. It then copies four bytes per configured human to the output and increments the global latest-available sequence. The bit meanings are not established.

The cross-path control at `DAT_006fd50c` remains deliberately unnamed. Its direct references include input submission/consumption, replicated vehicle updates, network motion/AI response, and replay/race-speech paths; writers include configuration/default loading, transport-menu/session setup and shutdown. In the input routines, nonzero selects local append and a local-row-only refresh branch, while other consumers' exact policies and the user-facing meaning remain unresolved. A repeatable Ghidra comment records this bounded cross-reference interpretation rather than assigning it one Boolean feature name. Static evidence only.

The caller supplies the builder an output pointer at stack offset `EBP-0x23`, immediately after the type byte at `EBP-0x24`, but transmits the complete 32-byte frame area regardless of the number of rows the loop writes. Full aligned caller assembly `004c60c0..004c61db` reserves `0x24` bytes and stores only the type byte before calling the builder; it contains no full-area clear. The builder copies four bytes per configured human row, so for N rows its direct writes cover `4*N` bytes of the 32-byte area. When N is below eight, the remaining tail is not assigned by these instructions. This is a static write-coverage observation only; the resulting values and any network-visible effect are not established. REA shipped-artifact dossier `ev_8297739b1daa2d11b37c3ffd643aff868c15ebd3ca252980d1de6cf125dc56cf` records the same target SHA-256 and full function body `004c60c0..004c61db`; its ephemeral generic naming is separate from the saved project annotations. The local roster producer `BuildAndBroadcastNetworkParticipantRoster` (`004a66c0`) initializes the participant count to one and scans exactly seven remote rows, incrementing for each active row; this locally constructed roster therefore has 1..8 participants under stable row state. Race-roster builders derive `g_nConfiguredHumanParticipantCount` from human racers in regular/mode-one/mode-two races and from human racers plus police in Hot Pursuit. However, `ReceiveNetworkParticipantRoster` (`004a68d0`) copies the fixed `0x7c`-byte roster, including its count, without locally normalizing that count. The local producer supports an eight-slot bound, but the received-count invariant across roles/transports is not established. Treat this as an unresolved frame-padding/participant-count contract, not as confirmed malformed-frame behavior or a runtime defect; trace all count writers/validators before drawing a broader conclusion.

The roster field is the signed WORD `g_nNetworkRosterParticipantCount` at `007a2276`, wire offset `+0x62` from the `007a2214` buffer. Code commonly reads the containing DWORD at `007a2274` and arithmetic-shifts by16, so negative advertised values remain signed in loop comparisons. The local producer writes the WORD directly; the receiver's fixed-size copy imports the field without normalization. This wire value is distinct from the derived `g_nConfiguredHumanParticipantCount` at `006fd514`; a local 1..8 producer result does not establish the received invariant or storage safety.

For the synchronized transport-1 receive layout, there is a conditional count-to-frame extent gap. `ReceiveNetworkParticipantRoster` copies the signed advertised count without normalization. In `BuildRegularRaceRoster` network modes2–4, the count loop at `00473d62` uses that signed count as its bound with no upper clamp, creates one participant setup record per iteration, then `00473e80` publishes the resulting human-racer count as `g_nConfiguredHumanParticipantCount`. When this machine later receives a type-6 host frame with host-role flag clear, `ReceiveNetworkBufferedInputMessage` uses that global as its four-byte sample loop count. The transmitted host frame contains only eight sample rows (32 bytes after the type byte); a count above8 makes this receiver read beyond the declared sample area. The local roster producer scans seven remote slots and emits1..8 entries under stable state, but the receiving copy and this builder do not enforce that range. This is a conditional static boundary, not evidence of a reachable malformed count or a runtime defect; sender/provider policy, race setup path and backing-storage consequences remain unresolved. Ghidra EOL comments at roster copy `004a6924`, publication `00473e80` and receiver loop `004c6219` record this chain. The correct count-loop instruction is `00473d62`. Follow-up live assembly inspection confirmed its DWORD load followed by SAR16/CMP/JGE; the EOL comment was added at that instruction, read back and saved successfully. Annotation correction DONE; admission/runtime questions remain open.

Its xref inventory also shows lifecycle values, so it is not invariably an already-advertised roster count: `ResetNetworkSessionState` and `InitializeNetworkSessionFromServiceSelection` store1; `InitializeNetworkClientAndAwaitRoster` stores0 before waiting; `ResetAndStartNetworkTransportTwoSession` stores1; `InitializeNetworkSessionTimingAndCounters` stores2; and `ServiceHostNetworkAdmissions` conditionally increments it after its status gate. The host roster producer resets it to1 and increments for each active remote row among its seven scanned slots. The receive handler then copies the wire field as part of the full roster. These distinct setup phases explain local values, but do not normalize received data or prove one invariant across transports and races.

`ReceiveNetworkParticipantRoster` (`004a68d0`) also uses `007a2210` as a first-receive lock flag: it acquires `0055ecb4` only when the flag is already nonzero, then sets the flag after the roster copy. Assembly clears eight WORDs at `g_nNetworkParticipantStates` (`007a22ca`), indices0..7 through `007a22d8`. The machine code addresses these as `[007a22c8 + 2*index]` for index1..8, leaving the preceding WORD at `007a22c8` unchanged. This reconciles the pseudocode's `g_nNetworkParticipantStates[0]` store with subsequent `g_nNetworkPeerSyncMarkers[9..15]` references: those indices exceed the marker array's declared extent, but their machine-code addresses lie in the adjacent participant-state array. They do not mean the machine code skips participant-state element0 or that the marker array has extra entries. The initial lock bypass and synchronization guarantees remain unresolved; the receiver still performs a fixed `0x7c` copy without a local packet-length or advertised-count check.

The full packet layout and related admission limits are indexed in the [network roster admission contract](network-roster-admission.md#roster-count-lifecycle).

The eight-byte identifier field at wire offset`+0x59` has a separate, evidence-backed role: the local producer writes the low byte returned by `GetNpsLocalUserIdLowByte` at index0 and appends active remote IDs under transport2; the receiver scans all eight positions, skips its own ID from that getter, and compacts remaining IDs into remote rows. The fixed scan is not driven by the advertised count. Identifier validity, uniqueness and consistency with the count are still unknown; no overall player-capacity inference follows.

The 88-byte name region is now typed as eight11-byte `Nfs3ParticipantNameSlot` entries. The primary profile-name prompt calls `CheckPlayerProfileNameLength`, which accepts nonempty NUL-terminated byte strings up to10 bytes; this fits a slot, though its localized fallback is not revalidated at that callsite. Network name-copy loops instead transfer byte pairs until either byte is NUL and have no local11-byte destination check. Host admission reads the name from the first11 bytes of a queued `PendingNetworkRequestRecord` and copies it to `007a25dc + 11*slot`; its NUL/length invariant is unproved. The copy base equals endpoint record7 (`007a22e8 + 7*0x6c`), and the host path scans/writes index7. In the separately documented all-eight-active fallthrough, the name copier receives slot8 and starts at base+88 before endpoint initialization. These are storage-alias/boundary candidates only: allocation extent, lifetime overlap and runtime consequence remain unverified. See the [network roster name contract](network-roster-admission.md#name-slot-width-and-copy-boundaries); retain remote-name admission and the index7/slot8 questions for Astra/runtime validation.

Other submit paths construct a six-byte type-6 message in global storage: type byte 6, one lead/high-water byte, then one four-byte input sample. Depending on transport and `006fd50c`, the function may append locally, skip transmission, or send this compact message. `ReceiveNetworkBufferedInputMessage` (`004c61e0`) is registered for type 6. With synchronization active, host-role flag clear plus transport 1 reads `g_nConfiguredHumanParticipantCount` four-byte rows from `packet+1+4*row`, matching the 32-byte data area of the host frame when count is at most eight. The alternate path sign-extends `packet[1]` as a high-water/lead value and reads one sample from `packet+2`; transport 1 resolves the sender and applies lead correction under the race-input lock, while other transports append to a selected local row. `DispatchNetworkControlPacket` (`004a6440`) reads the type and abort state but accepts no checked length argument, and this type-6 handler does not validate payload extent. `ReceiveNetworkParticipantRoster` copies the fixed roster including its advertised count without local normalization. The type-1 socket reader (`004f6640`) decodes a two-byte outer length, rejects values above `WORD[state+4]`, and requires an exact `length+2` peek before passing payload and length into unpacker chain `005126f0`/`00512650`/`005125b0` at index0. If the unpacker collection is empty, index0 is out of range and `005125b0` falls back to `00512470`, which flattens the descriptor and invokes connection+0x20; `004a6410` installs `004a6440` there. A populated index0 invokes its registered callback instead; whether it transforms or forwards type-6 data is unproved. A present-but-null slot takes the diagnostic path rather than the fallback. The outer length bound and exact-frame gate therefore apply only to this socket path; no positive or type-6-specific minimum is enforced in the documented chain, and actual input-provider coverage remains unknown. The type-1 opener sets connection state+4 in `InitializeSocketConnectionState` (`004f6c50`) from WORD `g_wWinsockImaxUdpDg` (`009f37e8`), the `WSAStartup` output at+0x188 matching legacy `WSADATA.iMaxUdpDg` ([Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsock/ns-winsock-wsadata)). Zero selects1024; nonzero stores low16(value-2) without a1024 cap. `InitializeSocketProviderLibrary` (`004f73a0`) reports a separate capacity capped at1024, but the constructor does not use that return for state+4. The startup request is0x0101; the runtime word, later mutation and actual stream-frame capacity are not established. Whether gameplay type-6 input uses this socket provider remains unresolved. Do not generalize this conditional socket evidence to every transport. The remaining facts leave transport-level framing and received-count admission as upstream questions; they do not by themselves establish malformed traffic or a runtime defect. Full cross-transport schema, scheduling and action-byte names remain unresolved. Static evidence only; no network or Wine test was performed.

Ghidra comments record the conditional mask at `004c6918`; the builder and submitter plates retain the custom ABI and scope limits. Project saved. No executable bytes or runtime memory were changed.

### Host network admission at a full endpoint table

`ServiceHostNetworkAdmissions` (`0049eae0`) dequeues a pending request, then scans endpoint active flags at indices0..7. Assembly `0049eb7f..0049eb88` exits with DX=8 when all eight are occupied and branches to common initialization rather than rejecting the request. The call at`0049ebec` passes that slot to `InitializeNetworkParticipantEndpoint` (`0049efb0`). The initializer sign-extends DX, computes `007a22e8 + slot*0x6c`, writes three WORDs at record+`0x2a/+0x2c/+0x2e`, then copies20 bytes at+`0x34`; it performs no slot-range check. The writes precede the later connection-layer result branch. The other caller, `JoinSelectedNetworkGameAndAwaitRoster` (`0049e800`), explicitly passes slot0.

Thus a pending request while every probed slot is active conditionally reaches slot8, one stride beyond the service's scanned index domain0..7. The producer `TryQueueNetworkAdmissionRequest` (`0049e320`) gates on a separate reservation counter below7 and increments it before enqueue. The six-record ring writer `EnqueuePendingNetworkRequest` (`0049f6a0`) advances modulo6 without a local full check. This gate may constrain pending-at-full-table reachability, but the counter is not compared with endpoint flags here. `HandleNpsConnectionEvent` (`004a5e50`) is stored at`004a5c16` in a callback record passed to the indirect `NPSConnectToServer` call; Ghidra has no internal invocation edge for that external callback. The admission service is called by `ProcessNetworkProfileAndRaceSettingChanges` (`0049a520`), whose sole direct caller is `RenderNetworkLobbyPanelAndProcessRaceStart` (`00441040`). These static paths do not establish callback dispatch timing, threading or serialization, so the cross-state invariant remains unresolved. Backing extent/adjacent ownership and downstream effects also remain open. Successful setup may increment the roster count, but the supported player total and whether this path is reachable in normal sessions are not established; nine-player support must not be inferred. Ghidra comments were saved. REA shipped-artifact dossier `ev_3cb033b36010cf0b2f88404a82e069596bfadace95f65f5e9640f30af738209` provides independent static body evidence. No network test or executable modification.

### Shared serial receive-count getter and provider adapters

Named `0051b8a0` as `GetSerialReceiveRingByteCount` after tracing the field through receive submission/completion and consumption. It takes a signed EAX serial-record index, lazily initializes and enters the shared critical section, calls `CheckSerialPortRecordExists` (index0..15 and nonnull table entry), then reads DWORD+0x10 of the pointed-to record or returns0. Lock exit occurs on both paths. EBX/ECX/EDX are preserved; the result is scalar EAX. Zero can mean an empty ring or an invalid/missing record, and lock lifecycle remains unresolved.

The two +0x38 forwarding wrappers now have provider-specific names from their sole direct callers: `004fa4f0 GetTapiModemReceivedByteCount` is called by `CheckType6TapiReceiveAvailability` (`004fa480`), while `004fa720 GetComProviderReceivedByteCount` is called by `CheckType3SerialReceiveAvailability` (`004fa6e0`). Each loads DWORD+0x38 from its provider record and tail-jumps to the shared count getter; neither checks for a null record. The caller callbacks poll the byte count and invoke their upper callback when nonzero; they do not consume the bytes. The names identify these callsite roles without asserting complete provider-record layouts or runtime availability. Ghidra comments were updated and saved; executable unchanged.

### TAPI call request setup (`004fa030`)

Renamed to `TryTapiMakeCall` after parent assembly review of Luna findings and inspection of `005311c0`, whose lazy export name is `lineMakeCall`. EAX supplies destination input; no stack inputs, all six non-EAX registers preserved. Null input or zero global `009f4da0` returns0. Diagnostics identify `TapiMakeCall` / `win_tapipkt.c`.

Allocates and zero-fills0x70 bytes, then sets DWORD offsets0/4/0x10/0x2c to0x70/1/0x10/3000. Query arguments are `([009f4da0],&009f4da4,destination,0,block)`; allocator/fill preserve carried ECX and free preserves its saved call result. After freeing, signed-negative result sets `009f4d9c=15` and returns0; nonnegative returns1. Acceptance does not prove connection. Packet field semantics, asynchronous completion, global lifecycle and runtime availability remain unresolved; no local allocation-null guard. Ghidra contains the same evidence boundaries.

### TAPI data-modem handle query (`004fa0f0`)

Renamed to `LoadTapiDataModemHandle` after full assembly review and inspection of lazy export wrapper `00530a4e`, which names `lineGetID`. Diagnostic strings identify `TapiGetModemHandle` and `win_tapipkt.c`; device class is `comm/datamodem`. No explicit inputs; all six non-EAX registers are preserved, plain RET. Scalar EAX is0 on success or-1 on query failure, rather than the decompiler longlong.

Allocates0x18 bytes, writes allocated size at+0, and queries with stack arguments `(0,0,[009f4da4],4,buffer,class)`. Zero query result with unsigned needed size+4 above allocated size frees and reallocates the requested extent, then retries. Otherwise it reads a DWORD at buffer plus offset stored+0x14 into global `009f4da8`, frees the buffer and returns0. Failure frees and returns-1 without clearing that global. No local allocation-null, offset/length, retry-limit or handle-validity checks; runtime availability is unproved. Matching ABI and limits are saved in Ghidra.

### Seven-slot payload insertion (`0049f5c0`)

Renamed to `InsertUnique20BytePayloadIntoSevenSlotTable` after independent assembly verification of the Luna review. EAX supplies a 20-byte payload; there are no stack arguments. The function preserves all six non-EAX general-purpose registers and returns a scalar EAX boolean, rather than the decompiler's inferred `undefined8` result.

It scans seven pointers at `007a02e8`. Occupied slots are compared by `004f5040` with descriptor `007a0390`, the incoming pointer in EDX and the existing pointer in EBX. Any nonzero result rejects insertion. Otherwise the first empty slot receives the address `007a0304 + index * 0x14`, and five DWORDs are copied into that row. EAX is 1 after insertion, or 0 after comparator rejection or a full table.

The uniqueness criterion belongs to the indirect comparator and remains unresolved. Payload fields and direct caller context are unknown; no protocol identity or runtime behavior is claimed. There are no local pointer/extent checks or replacement/removal operations. The same contract and limitations are recorded in the Ghidra plate comment.

### Network transport-selection menu initialization

- **Function:** `0043f320`, `InitializeNetworkTransportSelectionMenu`; data `005f3fe8` named `g_dwNetworkTransportMenuSelector`.
- **Evidence:** Luna review, independent full assembly `0043f320..0043f4d6`, decompiler and bounded `LookupLocalizedText` assembly. Fill wrapper preserves ECX; text IDs used here are all <=`0x7a2`, preserving EDX zero and ECX selector.
- **Contract:** EAX unsigned selector. Clears four menu storage blocks, fills IDs `15/1b..22/f9/c6`, stores selector. Selectors 0/1 set transport mode1 and secondary `006fd50c` zero; selector2 sets both zero; other values retain existing modes. Writes booleans at `005f3fe4` (transport zero) and `005f3fe0` (secondary zero), invokes toggle-menu helper with two-option counts and callback `0043f7e0`. Preserves EBX/ECX/EDX/ESI/EDI/EBP; no explicit status.

### Network connection-menu callbacks (`0043f640`, `0043f680`, `0043f7e0`, `0043fa00`)

- **Recovered callback entries:** `0043f640 HandleNetworkSetupMenuSelectionCallback` has a data reference from `0044006e` and opens `InitializeNetworkTransportSelectionMenu` for selected option0. `0043f680 HandleNetworkServiceSelectionCallback` is passed to menu initialization at `0043f51d`. `0043f7e0 HandleNetworkTransportMenuCallback` is explicitly passed to `InitializeFrontendToggleMenu` by `InitializeNetworkTransportSelectionMenu` at `0043f496`. `0043fa00 HandleNetworkSessionTextEntryCallback` is passed to the frontend menu initializer at `0043fb8e`. These four entries were embedded in larger unpartitioned code and lacked Ghidra function records; the explicit pointers, callback-shaped prologues/returns and bounded control flow support creating separate function boundaries.
- **Shared callback shape:** EAX carries the frontend event code and EDX points to a one-byte handled/result flag, as shown by each entry's stores and registration context. Event3 sets the byte; some callbacks also drain queued input on that path. Callback return values0 and5 are framework results; do not interpret them as network status.
- **Service-selection callback:** On event1 and selected option0, copies the dialog text to global `006fbb7e`, calls `BuildNetworkEndpointFromMutableAddress`, displays an untimed notice, pumps frontend frames, then calls `JoinSelectedNetworkGameAndAwaitRoster`. A successful join receives further timeout/frame servicing. Option1 marks the callback handled. The callback's apparent scalar result is callee/register-dependent and is not a network status. Exact string format, address semantics and service availability are unresolved.
- **Transport-menu callback:** On event1, selected option0 branches on `g_dwNetworkTransportMenuSelector`. Selector0/1 paths invoke `InitializeNetworkSessionFromServiceSelection` (selector0 also has a `0055eb2e & 0x10` branch that sets race mode3); selector2 sets session mode2 and host-role flag1, then calls `InitializeNetworkSessionConnection`, resetting session mode0 on failure. Successful setup pumps the frontend timeout/render path and returns5. A nonzero selected-option path handles option1 or clears one of the transport/secondary menu flags according to the hovered index. The exact labels, selector meanings and transport identities remain unresolved.
- **Text-entry callback:** On event1 and selected option0, copies the current dialog text to `006fbb60`, requires it to be nonempty, sets host-role flag0 and session mode2, then calls `InitializeNetworkSessionConnection`. Success services the frontend wait/render path and returns5; failure drains queued input and returns0. The text's encoding, semantic identity, destination capacity and actual endpoint remain unproved. The copy loop has no visible local destination bound; this alone does not establish reachable malformed input or a defect.
- **Evidence and limits:** Callback pointer references, full bounded disassembly and decompilation were reviewed. The installed `FEDATA/MENUS/connect.mnu` lists TCP, IPX, Modem, Serial and RaceNet entries, but does not map those labels to these callback selector values. This is legacy frontend/setup flow, not evidence of a currently reachable or functioning public lobby. Static analysis only; no live connection or endpoint behavior was tested, and no executable bytes changed.

### Modem-entry and COM-port selectors (`0043faf0`, `0043f960`)

- **Localized labels:** The installed English text table `fedata_org/text/text.eng` has a DWORD offset index; IDs `0x13` and `0x14` resolve to “Modem” and “COM Port”. These strings disambiguate two adjacent selector globals that earlier notes had conflated.
- **Modem list:** `0043faf0 HandleModemListSelectionMenuCallback` is a callback-shaped routine with an aligned prologue and standalone event branches; no direct registration xref is currently resolved. When signed count `g_nModemEntryCount` (`005f3df0`) is greater than1, menu option0 increments `g_nSelectedModemEntryIndex` (`006fbb5c`) with signed remainder modulo that count and refreshes the label. `BuildFrontendLocalizedIndexedLabel` (`0043f550`) prefixes localized ID`0x13` (“Modem”) and appends the indexed string from base `g_szModemEntryNameRows` (`005f3df4`) at stride`0x1e`. Only the first 30-byte row is typed; total table extent and schema are unknown. Other options open the phone-number text-entry callback or the transport menu. With count<=1, the menu takes a reduced path and avoids the modulo operation.
- **COM-port selector:** `0043f960 HandleComPortSelectionMenuCallback` is also callback-shaped, but its direct registration remains unresolved. Option1 increments `g_nSelectedComPortIndex` (`006fbb58`) with signed remainder modulo literal4 and updates the label. `0043f610 FormatComPortSelectionLabel` looks up localized ID`0x14` (“COM Port”) and formats `%s: %d` with the one-based selector value into shared buffer`005f403a`. Option0 sets session mode3 and attempts session initialization; callback result5 follows successful initialization. Default configuration initializes the selector to0.
- **Installed menu dispatch boundary:** `FEDATA/MENUS/connect.mnu` uses `[button]` entries with `codelink=modem` or `serial` and `nextmenu=mainmult`. `ParseBracketedMenuCommandId` resolves `[button]` to registry ID5 at `00557aa8`; its template `00556e40` stores `HandleFrontendButtonInput` (`00461270`) at `+0x30`. The field-definition row at `00557c50` parses `codelink` as a type-4 arena-string pointer at menu-item `+0x10`; the `nextmenu` row at `00557e10` stores a separate string pointer at `+0x40`. For a simple button with template fields `+0x58` and `+0x64` zero, the handler recognizes `racenow` and `exit`; another codelink with a nonnull `nextmenu` takes generic action5, which `RunFrontendMenuLoop` resolves as a menu descriptor transition. Thus the installed modem/serial entries establish a generic transition to `mainmult`, not a direct dispatch to either specialized selector callback. Fresh Ghidra readback shows no xrefs to `0043faf0` or `0043f960`; their registration and any indirect/external route remain unresolved. Ghidra comments were saved on the template/field rows and all three handlers. REA string evidence independently correlates the installed tokens with in-image strings at `00537908` and `00537910` (Evidence `ev_8abd884828486edd63debeb29f1fb437fb9b6339669078f51ce8885983299f7e`, `ev_af2e02f7b11e0c29e567748ee6a7b858a58236e16c7ea17b2118ba3851809b9a`); token matching alone does not prove callback registration.
- **Selector-to-session-record dataflow:** `InitializeNetworkSessionConnection` (`004c3f90`) carries its incoming EAX value into `InitializeNetworkSessionTimingAndCounters` (`004c4230`). For session state1, that initializer copies incoming EAX through EDX (preserved by `InitializeNetworkPacketState`) and stores it at `007a2324`; `HandleNetworkSessionTextEntryCallback` supplies `g_nSelectedModemEntryIndex`. `HandleNetworkTransportMenuCallback` (`0043f7e0`) supplies a second explicit UI path: in selected-option0 with `g_dwNetworkTransportMenuSelector==2`, it stores session mode2, loads `g_nSelectedModemEntryIndex` into EAX at `0043f8a4`, and calls `InitializeNetworkSessionConnection` (`004c3f90`). That callee maps mode2 to network session state1, then forwards EAX to the timing initializer. The state-1 setup passes record `007a22e8` to `InitializeConnectionRecordType6Defaults` (`004fa550`), where `+0x3c` is consumed by `HandleTapiModemCallWorker` as the argument to `SelectTapiModemRecordByIndex`. Together with `HandleNetworkSessionTextEntryCallback`, this establishes two static call paths from the selected modem index to the TAPI record selector; it does not establish that the displayed modem-name rows are populated from, or ordered like, the separate TAPI table. For every other session state, the timing initializer loads `g_nSelectedComPortIndex` and stores it at `007a2320`; the COM-port menu chooses state2. The type-3 setup passes record `007a22e8` to `InitializeConnectionRecordType3Defaults`; its `+0x38` is exactly `007a2320`. See [type-3 serial-provider callback](#type-3-serial-provider-callback-and-com-port-field) and [type-6 TAPI provider](#type-6-tapi-modem-provider-and-selected-index-handoff).
- **COM device-number mapping:** The COM selector is copied to type-3 session-record `+0x38` (`007a2320`). `OpenAndConfigureSerialConnection` passes that zero-based value to `OpenIndexedSerialPortDevice`, which formats `\\.\\COM%d` with `index+1`. The four menu values0..3 therefore request COM1..COM4. The generic helper's local table/path range is0..15 (COM1..COM16); this path-format mapping does not establish that the requested OS device exists or opens.
- **Limits:** The UI modem-name rows/count (`005f3df4`/`005f3df0`) and TAPI enumerated record table/count (`009f4d94`/`009f4d80`) are separate globals. Both UI globals are in `.bss`; the current direct-xref inventory shows no writer for the UI count or rows, and the runtime values/population path are not established. An independent shipped-artifact REA/Ghidra cross-check found one direct count reference, `0043fb30`, and instruction evidence identifies it as `MOV ECX,[005f3df0]` (Evidence `ev_6955640b66bfdb73b1c358f13439b78fb92ddcd1c560cfb2f631f5cdb39a9206`, `ev_22b07c52908481fa4018c3df0d50a73c5af432e10c430825ae6219ee34e3d450`). The table-base references at `0043f5b8` and `0043f5e1` are address materialization in the label formatter, not direct stores (Evidence `ev_9f086622cda61bdcba5f5a2a5fea11715f738b7baa3d71ea2b94673129a1732`, `ev_76e72587dfad1e2a9104d8495122ec498c3d3d784aa28915392f2ed7c52e3806`, `ev_c79327c4cacc6f1a1f7227f922d1cc1cbb6398cc756a961989b051c05360b1ca`). These direct-reference results do not exclude indirect writes or identify an external/indirect population path. Although the selected modem index reaches `SelectTapiModemRecordByIndex`, the identity, ordering and count correspondence between displayed names and TAPI records remain unproved. The installed `connect.mnu` codelink tokens `modem` and `serial` correlate with in-image strings at `00537908` and `00537910` (REA Evidence `ev_8abd884828486edd63debeb29f1fb437fb9b6339669078f51ce8885983299f7e`, `ev_af2e02f7b11e0c29e567748ee6a7b858a58236e16c7ea17b2118ba3851809b9a`), but Ghidra has no direct xrefs to those token strings or to either callback entry. This text correlation does not establish callback registration. Actual modem semantics and runtime connection behavior remain unverified. Static code and installed text evidence only; no executable bytes changed.

### Participant state control-message sender

- **Function:** `004c7ea0`, `SendParticipantStateControlMessages` (formerly `FUN_004c7ea0`).
- **Contract:** When `006fd50c != 0` and signed session mode is greater than one, brackets transmission with synchronization markers `(0x5a,0x22)` and `(0x5a,0x23)`. Builds a `0xc4`-byte type-`0x0c` control message containing a participant byte and `0xc0` bytes copied from object offset `0x224`.
- **Evidence:** Assembly `004c7ee8..004c7f01` obtains the first object from `005efa48[index]`. The host-only loop `004c7f1f..004c7f6b` uses a **different table**, `005efac8[index]`, iterating from configured human count to configured participant count, skipping null entries. Periodic callbacks run before each loop send. Both sends use `SendNetworkControlMessage` with connection argument zero.
- **Limits:** Header bytes 2 and 3 are not initialized locally. The selected-object path has no local null/index guard. Complete payload schema, table equivalence, receiver padding interpretation and synchronization guarantees are not established. Register ABI retained because pseudocode omits important arguments.
- **Validation:** Static disassembly and helper pseudocode reviewed; name and plate comment saved in Ghidra. No runtime test or executable modification.

The receive-side match is now checked at the control table's slot12 (`0055ecec` contains pointer `004c7f90`): `ApplyNetworkVehicleStateBlock` reads packet byte `+1` as a vehicle-table index, loads `g_pRaceVehiclesByMasterIndex[index]` from `005efac8`, and copies `0xc0` bytes from packet `+4` to vehicle `+0x224`. This matches the sender's participant byte and 192-byte source block. If session flag `007a22da` is nonzero, the handler passes the same packet pointer and full `0xc4` length to the transport helper. The identified handler ignores packet header bytes `+2/+3`, although a relay preserves them. No local payload-length, table-index, or null-entry check precedes the copy; the byte index can address beyond the 16-entry master table, and short payloads would not satisfy the fixed copy extent. Upstream framing/admission and actual delivery remain unresolved, so these are conditional static boundaries, not demonstrated runtime faults. The sender's only direct caller is `BuildRaceResultSnapshotsAndUpdateProgression` (`00455410`); this call graph does not establish per-frame transmission. Evidence: sender assembly `ev_9027b9449fc6f122e8a1b5334962fd28bad11a13827f3afde077b4f9824e7b7a`, caller pseudocode `ev_3106f89c55e9339f704d61b059327b7ed260ac8a4023398362ac5a170c7de6e7`, slot bytes/xref `ev_6a11b652a483888568f09cf1936517f4aac982068a5b299f37edd9cc93edcfc5` / `ev_805f296d3bab80d6aab755203cdd5ce903e62361263b6106ec8772186269cad7`, and receiver instruction observations `ev_0ac76b2351ba32dcb7bdfe91288ed6f8c3180758093beca1baf29283228cd1bf`, `ev_31232a0c4a4362d1a07203d8fd117f97b4d400fe470d765f88e303a2bba5f211`, `ev_4ce6687ba9ed240e4a8b31954c69464f3bd4d8afc8c55d65bcc51b59d6d3a2b8`, `ev_acb7ac313b426209372586a504feddafcdb2772f9586af82047968ede6053e84`, `ev_8c9280263d239f95ad1876e7252b05338b348819d0281883c9620ade2b6ddd17`, `ev_c4dd6bba45ac9fa6cf84f50fa2f2bcbe2ab0346dadadf3ce92a269626072d365`, and `ev_8f4fba5d13d43ccdd30e21060f52def6b4bfde205e1dd8f348ead4f76c54fdb4`.

### Draining buffered stream packets (`00495b30`)

`DrainBufferedStreamQueuePackets` retains the EAX stream/queue handle in ECX, repeatedly calls `TakeBufferedStreamQueuePacket`, and exits on null. Each nonnull packet is passed in EDX to `ReleaseBufferedStreamPacketAndResumeRefill` with the original handle in EAX. Both callees preserve ECX, sustaining the loop handle. The wrapper restores ECX/EDX/EBP and returns EAX=0 on normal exit, with plain RET and no stack arguments.

Release can resume refill, so this is not proved to drain only a fixed entry snapshot or always terminate under arbitrary producer behavior. Full queue/concurrency invariants remain deferred. Name/comment were read back and Ghidra saved; executable bytes remain unchanged.

### Current tracked-entry lookup (`00495890`)

- **Name:** `GetCurrentTrackedEntryOrNull`.
- **Verified assembly:** reads the index at `0079f354` and end/count marker at `0079f358`. Equality returns zero; otherwise EAX receives the DWORD at `0079f294 + index * 8`. No memory writes, calls, or stack arguments; EDX and EBP are preserved.
- **Limit:** the end test checks equality only, not whether the index exceeds the marker. The tracked entries' full domain and lifecycle remain unresolved. This is a static contract, without new runtime validation.

### Ordered tracked-entry insertion (`004958c0`)

- **Name:** `InsertTrackedEntryBySignedKey`.
- **Verified assembly:** EAX supplies a signed key. The routine retains the paired DWORD at `0079f294 + 8*n`, where `n` is `0079f354`, then shifts preceding 8-byte records right while their keys are greater than or equal to the new key. Records start at `0079f290`; the new key and retained paired value occupy the resulting insertion slot. Equal keys precede existing equals. Finally it increments `0079f354` and returns the insertion index in EAX.
- **ABI and limits:** no stack arguments or calls; preserves EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI, EDI and EBP. The MOVSD copies assume a clear direction flag. No explicit capacity check against `0079f358` is present. Sorted-prefix and valid-index assumptions, and the records' full domain/lifecycle, remain caller responsibilities requiring further analysis.

### Signed parameter and tick initialization (`00495a10`)

- **Name:** `InitializeSignedParameterAndTickState`.
- **Verified assembly:** stores incoming EAX at `0079f33c`, sets `0079f338` to one for a signed nonnegative input and zero otherwise, calls `ReadMultimediaTickCount` (`004f2790`, imported `timeGetTime`), stores the DWORD tick at `0079f328`, and clears DWORDs `0079f320` and `0079f318`.
- **ABI:** no stack arguments; EAX retains the sampled tick on return. EDX and EBP are saved/restored; the clock wrapper also preserves ECX/EDX. Other nonvolatile registers are untouched locally.
- **Boundary:** the input's full meaning and the cleared fields' roles in caller `00495bc0` remain unresolved. Naming deliberately describes the proven effects rather than assigning a playback mode or clock policy. No runtime test performed.

### Dispatching an ordered prefix with payload recycling (`00495920`)

- **Name:** `DispatchLatestTrackedEntryThroughSignedKey`.
- **Selection:** EAX is a signed threshold. A zero active count (`0079f354`) or threshold below the first key returns zero without local writes or calls. Otherwise signed comparisons identify a prefix of length `k` whose final key is at or below the threshold. The final record's paired DWORD is passed to `004df2b0`; that callee preserves ECX/EDX, while its larger dispatch effects remain unresolved here.
- **Updates:** increments `0079f340`, adds `threshold - selected_key` to `0079f35c`, and adds `k - 1` to `0079f360`, with DWORD arithmetic. Active count decreases by `k`; success returns one.
- **Important compaction detail:** the loop uses `0079f358 - k`, not the active count. For each destination slot `j`, it saves that slot's paired value, copies the two DWORDs from slot `j+k` down to `j`, then writes the saved paired value back to source slot `j+k`. This recycles paired values across the full slot range; describing it as an ordinary active-record memmove would lose behaviour.
- **ABI and limits:** no stack arguments; preserves EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI, EDI and EBP. Sorted-prefix/bound invariants and a clear direction flag are assumed. Full entry domain, dispatcher lifecycle and runtime behaviour remain unvalidated.

### Tracked-entry count globals (`0079f354`, `0079f358`)

- `g_nTrackedEntryActiveCount` (`0079f354`, signed int): zeroed by `004957a0`, incremented by insertion, reduced by dispatched prefix length, and used as the next available slot index by the current-entry getter.
- `g_nTrackedEntrySlotCount` (`0079f358`, signed int): configured from the initializer's first stack argument and used for allocation, cleanup and full-range payload recycling. The initializer diagnoses signed values greater than 16 but contains no local clamp; full caller validation remains unresolved.
- Cross-references distinguish the active sorted prefix from the full slot range. The getter compares these counts for equality only. These names describe the verified storage roles without asserting the entries' full domain or safe bounds for arbitrary inputs.

### Freeing tracked-entry payloads (`00495860`)

- **Name:** `FreeTrackedEntryPayloads`.
- **Verified assembly:** signed loop from zero to `g_nTrackedEntrySlotCount` passes each paired DWORD at `0079f294 + 8*i` to `FreeMemoryPoolBlock` (`004e1890`). That callee preserves EDX, which carries the loop index. Free results are ignored.
- **Final call:** always calls `004df310`, including for a nonpositive slot count. That helper compares `004eba80`'s result with `008ca2c0`; on a match with nonnull `008ca2c8`, it invokes the object's vtable slot at `+8` and clears `008ca2c8`. The full object domain and ownership remain unresolved.
- **Limits and ABI:** no stack arguments; EDX/EBP saved and restored. No meaningful return is explicitly constructed. The helper does not locally clear payload pointers or either entry count, so repeated-call safety or reset-to-empty behaviour is not established. No runtime test performed.

### In-place record CRC and masked offset helper

- **Recovered callback functions:** `0051d000` `ReadRecordSequenceKey` (4 bytes, returns record+4), `0051d010` `DecrementRecordCountdownAndTestExpired` (35 bytes, decrements positive+8 and returns whether resulting count<=0), and `0051d040` `FinalizeRecordWhenCountdownExpired` (16 bytes, positive count returns1 without action; otherwise tail-calls finalizer). Ghidra had no function definitions at these addresses. Referenced addresses, complete assembly and dry-run body extents verified before defining them. Callback references include0051d99b/0051d9a9; runtime cadence remains unresolved.

- **`0051cf30` → `ReadAndProcessBufferedRecords`:** callbacks byte+1f nonzero clears buffered count but still proceeds into read admission. Capacity>count admits callback+14, whose return is added without a local range/sign check. Parser0051cd50 receives remaining bytes and a local result pointer; after positive consumption, loop continuation checks underlying owner+24, not remaining count. The callback flag suppresses returned-length accounting/compaction when set. On ordinary exit consumed bytes are removed with memmove. Boolean return reflects parser-writable local result, not directly byte count. Exact flag meaning, parser bounds and callback lifetime remain open. Full assembly corrected two misleading high-level interpretations: initial flag does not skip reading, and positive consumption alone does not govern continued parsing.

Destination-node identity therefore depends on callback EDX preservation. Existing broader unlink/callback/lifetime deferral remains; generic name retained and plate corrected to expose this assumption.

No special case for head sentinelFFFFFFFF. Does not remove/requeue or update threshold. Query and lookup are separately locked, and lookup releases the lock before the node write; lifetime remains a caller obligation. EAX is not a stable status, particularly with diagnostics enabled. Rejected updates still run the transfer loop. While queue+54 head key<=threshold, pops and pushes to the head of queue+38; a sequence of moved nodes is therefore reversed at the destination head. Query/pop/push lock independently, with no enclosing transaction; concurrency eligibility and ownership remain unresolved. Empty-keyFFFFFFFF usually stops, except thresholdFFFFFFFF permits a terminating NULL pop. No node free or protocol-completion claim. Full assembly and queue helpers verified.

- **`0051caf0` → `ServiceRecordMarkerCountdown`:** NULL state returns1. Otherwise decrements state+8 with DWORD wrap, then tests the old signed value: positive returns1 without writing; nonpositive invokes the marker helper using pointer[context+18] and state+4 masked to7bits. Old1 therefore becomes0 but does not write until a later call. Result1 is not proof of a write. Negative counters are not clamped; callback cadence and runtime registration remain unresolved (Ghidra reported no direct callers). Assembly0051caf0–0051cb47 verified.

- **`0051ca50` → `WriteSixByteMarkerRecord`:** record+8 becomes1 before capacity-like query. If query result<6, return is callback EDX (initialized0), not an independently normalized Boolean. Otherwise builds FE,0,low8(marker),queue predecessor,CRC at record+0c and invokes writer for6 bytes. Exact6 returns1; only original marker<=127 additionally stamps+8 from underlying object WORD+2c. Other write results return0; bytes remain mutated. Caller0051caf0 masks marker to7bits and loads record pointer from `[context+18]`, not an embedded record. Callback preservation/lifecycle and protocol remain qualified. Full assembly verified.

- **`0051c8f0` → `FinalizeRecordAndInvokeWriteCallback`:** EAX record, EDX context. Query callback+0c must return an unsigned value at least byte(record+0d)+6; otherwise result0 and record+8=1. Admitted path updates+0f from0051c820 and CRC over record+0c (checksum lands at+10/+11), then invokes callback+18 with underlying context object, record+0c and that byte-derived length. Exact-length return gives1 and stamps record+8 from underlying object WORD+2e; any other return gives0/+8=1. Mutations persist on write failure. No claim of peer delivery, callback identity, partial-write recovery or universal input bounds. Live ECX preservation is an indirect-callback ABI expectation. Full assembly verified.

- **`0051c890` → `InitializeRecordHeaderAndCopyPayload`:** EAX destination, EDX context, EBX source, ECX byte count. Under context+54 queue lock, copies old context+30 sequence into record+4 and increments the counter. After unlock, writes sentinel+8=-1, marker+0c=FE, length+0d=low8(count), sequence+0e=low7(counter), then memmoves the full count into record+12. No local size guard; truncated stored length and full copy count must not be conflated. CRC/finalization and queue insertion are later caller operations (raw call0051d898). Exact protocol identity remains unresolved.

- **`0051c820`, generic name retained:** queries queue at object+78, falls back to object+74 on key-1, then decrements. Copies WORD[[object]+2a] to object+2c. Only AL is normalized to `(key-1)&0x7f`; upper EAX bits differ across diagnostic paths. Queue locking covers the key query only. - **`0051c7f0` → `RecomputeAndCompareRecordCrc16`:** saves original checksum bytes+4/+5, recomputes in place, returns1 for equality or0 otherwise. The original checksum is never restored, including on mismatch. EAX buffer and EDX length; EBX/ECX preserved, EDX retains the new CRC. Complete assembly `0051c7f0–0051c811` verified. No local extent checks; enclosing protocol/scanner ownership remains unresolved.

- **`0051c7c0` → `RecomputeRecordCrc16InPlace`:** EAX buffer, EDX byte length. Clears bytes+4/+5, calls the independently verified FBEA-seeded CRC helper, stores the result big-endian at+4/+5. Actual return residue is EAX=CRC>>8 and EDX=full CRC, not a Boolean. These two bytes are written even if length<6; there is no local extent guard. Protocol identity and validation ownership remain separate.

EAX result; EBX mask increments only on the adjustment branch; ECX preserved and EDX unchanged. Inspected callers use mask0x7f, but the entry's contract is broader than a low-seven-bit name would imply.
- **Validation:** complete assembly for both small bodies and existing CRC callee contract. Ghidra plates saved; no runtime or executable changes for these helpers.

### Serial transmit capacity and guarded enqueue

- **`0051b900` → `GetSerialTransmitRingFreeSpace`:** locked valid-port query returns512 minus record+234 queued count; invalid port returns0. DWORD subtraction is not clamped. EBX/ECX/EDX preserved.

- **Evidence and limits:** complete assembly plus existing record validator/transmit-ring contracts. Lazy lock initialization and lifetime remain unresolved; no serial-port runtime test. Ghidra names and comments saved.

## Cars, archives and resource loading

### Car registry, lookup and selector capacity are separate

`RecountCarModelRecords` (`00438be0`) walks the complete linked list and stores its count in `g_nCarModelRecordCount` (`005f3cc8`) without a local 50-record cap. The index API is narrower: `GetCarModelRecordByIndex` (`00439a50`) rejects signed indices above49 and uses the 50-pointer `g_pCarModelIndexCache` (`005f3c00`); negative indices are not rejected before cache addressing. A fresh REA/Ghidra dossier for the same shipped-artifact SHA-256 (`ev_49610379d6d16425f99ae3ca18f8aecd47570261af8c5dde4278f326a5dc8fc1`) confirms the complete body `00439a50..00439aa4`: signed `JLE` admits negative indices through the upper-only `index <= 49` test, and the getter uses `index*4` for both cache read and write. Its reference-manager result lists 40 resolved direct callers (`ev_2f56ec7029e305bdcfaee905f2400aa11101fa1330e39308f13b3db3aced00a6`); indirect callers are outside that count. The recount therefore must not be mistaken for the maximum model index, and the getter's boundary is shared well beyond the frontend selector.

The frontend selector adds a separate structure. `RebuildEligibleCarModelGroups` (`0043a580`) scans the recount minus `g_nCarModelCountAdjustment`, filters candidate records, and appends to a selector-derived group and a combined group. The adjustment is a DWORD with value1; current xrefs show reads at `0043a58f` and `0043a6f0`, with no code write found. A same-SHA shipped-artifact REA/Ghidra read observes bytes `01 00 00 00` at `00554f50` (Evidence `ev_c80392bf0cc38b1e8ddaea21b7cdfe11491b817d5521255bf97b9a73aed0f0a5`), the getter dossier confirms `GetCarModelCount` returns the linked-list count at `005f3cc8` (`ev_68fed0c64cfc8715e1358630cc9d9206d68560562266921fbfe3a024df0e8db8`), and instruction evidence confirms the subtraction at `0043a58f` (`ev_9eb025d854a970f407c99e00044047868c88255baeb097a0df2d6f338061e414`). Its role is mechanically a count adjustment, but the reason for subtracting one and the identity of any omitted record are unknown. If the linked-list count were50, this scan would process49 ordinals (0..48), which could coincide numerically with the reported 49-car user limit; the evidence does not prove that the registry normally reaches50 or that this arithmetic explains that report. This scan is independent of `GetCarModelRecordByIndex` (`00439a50`) and its 50-pointer cache, which accepts indices0..49. Its signed loop bound is not clamped: a negative count-minus-adjustment skips filtering/appends after the groups are cleared, but all four sort calls still run. Assembly-reviewed comments document four 50-pointer regions beginning at`005552d8`, adjacent counts at`005555f8`, and no local selector-domain or per-group count<50 guard. Slot-50 writes can alias neighboring group/count storage under the recorded layout. The selector-field provenance and selected-installation values are traced below; this does not establish that ordinary execution reaches an over-cap count or group write.

The source of the selector is now statically established. `DiscoverAndLoadCarModelRegistry` (`00439d90`) reads the FEDATA DWORD at`+8`, arithmetic-shifts right16, and stores the sign-extended high WORD at model-record `+0x388` (`0043a171`). `ApplyCarSelectionEligibilityMask` (`0043a6e0`) compares the raw value against0,1,2; `RebuildEligibleCarModelGroups` adds1 to form category indices1..3, while category0 is the combined list. A read-only inventory of the selected installation covers58 VIV archives,139 supported-language FEDATA members and24 model directories: selector counts are0:9,1:7,2:7 and255:1, with all six recognized language variants agreeing per model. `KNOC` is the outlier: its six localized FEDATA entries carry selector255, which would derive category index256. Its16-byte identifier is built-in ID33, but the source words mapped by the loader to model flags01,04 and40 are all zero; the ordinary built-in eligibility route requires flag40, so KNOC fails that route. It could still enter the group builder through the selected-human fallback in session0/1, subject to earlier police/mode gates. Thus the inventory establishes an installed exceptional value and a conditional static path, not loader/runtime reachability or an observed out-of-range write. The [retained report](evidence/inventories/installed-car-selector-categories.json) is reproducible with [the helper](scripts/inventory_car_selector_categories.py); its supported suffixes come from the executable language table and it excludes loose files, other FEDATA suffixes, alternate roots and modified assets. The Ghidra listing now names/types `g_pEligibleCarModelGroupEntries` as 200 `BYTE *` entries and `g_nEligibleCarModelGroupCounts` as four integers. No executable bytes were modified.

The fresh REA/Ghidra loader dossier (`ev_d839de47b9f466a5fb4d8c17222972c3b5d2871735a13217dd6a704ff23d590c`) identifies body entry `00439d90`, including the later initialization ranges. Model records are linked through helper `00438b90` (`ev_27eab62a57b54268c11ad1401f81e50675560149388b920e2079e6266a50d899`), whose body traverses to the list tail and links the new node without a local 50-entry check. `RecountCarModelRecords` (`00438be0`) counts that linked list and stores the result (`ev_46e4ff10b7a4abe260973c7252d012deccf72e29fbf8c3093570039238ea83bd`). After discovery, the loader uses this count in two ascending index loops without a 50-slot clamp. In the first loop, `0043a3a6` calls `GetCarModelRecordByIndex`, then `0043a3af` calls helper `004396b0`; that helper calls the getter again and immediately reads record+`0x380` without a null test (`ev_a77989af6c43110f879910c1986d44cb5a66d5c82ad9a52bf07391ee4252431c`). At index50 the getter's signed `JLE` guard returns null, so a registry count above50 conditionally reaches a null-derived read in this initialization pass. This is static control/data-flow evidence, not an observed crash; more-than50 record reachability remains unproven.

The loader's later `CheckCarModelIdentifiersUnique` (`00439d20`) uses the same full count as its loop bound and obtains each identifier through `GetCarModelIdentifier` (`00439520`). That helper adds`0x31c` to the record returned by the index getter without a null check. Because the index getter rejects indices above49, a loaded count above50 would also send this scan beyond the getter's supported ordinal range before the 16-byte comparison. The loader's ability to admit more than50 records is not established, so both paths remain conditional static boundaries rather than reported runtime failures.

Ghidra now defines `UpdateCarVivArchiveAndRefreshRegistry` (`0043ae60..0043b29c`, 1,085 bytes) from a conventional register-save/frame prologue through its shared epilogue. EAX supplies a model-identifier string; EDX is passed as the resource ID to `GetCarResourceDirectoryById`. The body creates a temporary car-resource directory, copies/edits `car.viv`, tries `fedata.%s` entries for up to seven configured languages, appends the supplied identifier to matching archive entries, creates/stores a GUID, rebuilds/writes the archive, and then reloads the car registry. Ghidra locals now name `modelIdentifier` as `char *` and the two values returned/retained from `FindBigfArchiveEntryByName` as opaque `void *` entry pointers; no full BIGF entry structure was inferred. These operation labels are based on the helper calls and embedded strings; exact file format validity and successful disk behavior were not tested. No direct incoming xref to the entry was found, so indirect dispatch and runtime reachability remain unknown. The Ghidra plate comment records this contract and the custom register-argument caveat.

Within that body, after `DiscoverAndLoadCarModelRegistry` returns its observed success value, the code calls `FindCarModelIndexByName` (`00439b20`) with the supplied name. That helper returns`-1` when a nonempty list is exhausted without a match (`00439b55–00439b5d`). The caller compares EAX with`-1` at`0043b27c`, but does not branch on the result; it passes the unchanged value to `GetCarModelRecordByIndex` (`00439a50`). The getter uses signed `JLE` for `index <= 49`, so`-1` passes the guard and addresses cache slot`-1` at`005f3bfc`, four bytes before the 50-entry cache at`005f3c00`. If that preceding DWORD is zero, the getter walks the list, reaches its end without matching the negative ordinal, and writes NULL back to the same preceding slot. If it is nonzero, the getter returns that DWORD as though it were a cached record pointer. A Ghidra data-region readback classifies the preceding 48-byte span (`005f3bd0..005f3bff`) as undefined with no static xrefs; `005f3bfc` has no data label/comment, and its uninitialized BSS value is unavailable. Its owner and contents therefore remain unknown; this is not evidence of unused padding. The lookup path is statically present in the newly defined function, but function reachability and the name-lookup failure condition remain unverified. This does not establish an ordinary gameplay failure or justify a broader car-slot conclusion.

For issue #4, treat the reported 49-car behavior as a question spanning these independent constraints, not as proof that any one array is the universal car-slot cap. The loader appends accepted unique records, recounts the list, and reorders groups without deleting nodes; its two following initialization loops use the full `GetCarModelCount`. The `C-1` scan is therefore a later selector-table rule, not an observed load-time record drop or 50-entry admission guard. The record at final ordinal `C-1` depends on the effective loaded/reordered registry and is not identified by this static trace. A safe expansion bound cannot be inferred until registry admission, selector categories, all array consumers and effective installed/runtime populations are reconciled. Ghidra comments were reviewed and saved; this is static evidence only, with no executable or runtime-memory change.

### Car registry cleanup and ordering helpers

`DiscoverAndLoadCarModelRegistry` begins at `00439d90`; its instruction at `00439d9e` calls `ResetCarModelIndexCache` (`004399f0`). The cleanup/rebuild helper at `00438eb0` also resets that cache, then partitions the current linked list before publishing a rebuilt head at `00554f70`. Its first pass (`00438e30`) extracts records whose category at `+0x388` is not `0xff` and whose flags byte at `+0x380` has neither bit `0x10` nor `0x08`; the next pass (`00438d60`) extracts bit-`0x10` records; the third (`00438dc0`) extracts category-`0xff` records. It appends those groups in that order, then appends the remaining list. Category and flag meanings are not inferred here. Dossiers: loader `ev_d839de47b9f466a5fb4d8c17222972c3b5d2871735a13217dd6a704ff23d590c`, rebuild `ev_a1f3d4673d3f1c8d08f4c6b0c7d8420d78dde1eaa030dc8ee7e983063b36722d`, and partition helpers `ev_079465fd94f60b5763b278fe812aa6635402dc1f032a7930a0ebe12b67dacd16`, `ev_5a5e0e1b589830818e1278175d02b973c5583bd9587cb5330198b721a3d6d576`, `ev_15932b944a2c631b7414d10aba70e60ac15f74684a21db81119b24f393bf2a86`.

The adjacent accessors clarify the interface. `00439ab0` takes the car-model ordinal in EAX and metadata-string ordinal in EDX; it returns the requested string pointer or the empty-string fallback at `00537690`. ### Frontend car-color selector callbacks

The 12 file-backed bytes at `005577fc` form three consecutive 32-bit code pointers: `00456ce0`, `00457030`, and `004571e0` (REA byte dossier `ev_e2f607f5349f0e651a484e00c359970ec68c2a15ed35334de3847eccbc5b2ed3`; REA xrefs to the first two entries are `ev_d2aecb670e1e8df8bc17a69a64a8a5b279f3aa098d44b8932842d22e002f285d` and `ev_45656be71a39d17aee810a40aa5adeb0451eff1db4e549f7269d5609db4e722c`; the third has xrefs `ev_c5be12600b3e95e62c9e4b2d3753ac7334140ee1549c45c0df21ad5ec929b552`). The project now labels the table `g_pFrontendCarColorSelectorCallbacks` and types it as three `void *` entries: the callbacks have distinct custom register contracts, so a uniform function-pointer prototype would overstate the evidence.

Two pointed-to routines were absent from the FunctionManager despite conventional prologues/epilogues and table references. They are now defined and decompiled in Ghidra: `UpdateAndRenderFrontendCarColorSelector` at `00456ce0–00456e97` and `HandleFrontendCarColorSelectorInput` at `00457030–004571d0`. The third entry, `UpdateFrontendColorSelectorLayout`, already existed at `004571e0–0045724d`.

`UpdateAndRenderFrontendCarColorSelector` takes the context in EAX and a render gate in EDX. It checks frontend-entry eligibility and a model-ID cell at context+`0x54`, synchronizes the selector state bit at byte +`0x05` from WORD +`0x58`, and refreshes the selection if the selected model ID at +`0x60` differs from that cell. With the render gate set, the active selector updates row +`0x48` from the cursor only when the cursor rectangle and row bounds pass, then draws the panel and one row per count at +`0x4c`. In the inactive state it delegates shape rendering; it also draws the selected palette item when global `00559c60` is zero. Observed paths return zero. The context structure and precise UI meanings for these fields remain unresolved.

`HandleFrontendCarColorSelectorInput` takes the context in EAX and event code in BX. When selector WORD +`0x58` is zero, event values `0x000d` and `0x4d00` enter color-edit mode. In the active state, `0x4800` and `0x5000` move the selected row, while `0x001b` cancels. The confirmation/click path checks the cursor rectangle, commits the selection, and may update menu focus when the committed selector matches the selected row. Handled paths return 2; ignored events return 0. These numeric codes are retained without assuming keyboard labels. Count-zero behavior and context layout remain unresolved.

The palette-helper caller paths and selector-range limits are detailed in the preceding registry/accessor discussion and in the Ghidra plate/EOL comments. Ghidra saved the updated project after the new function definitions and annotations; the function count increased from 4,311 to 4,313. The target executable's recorded SHA-256 remains `2a20f80465ed53d320f1a6f41c9dde2c07de0bc5525af1f23f8e6aff3e6181fb`. No runtime test was performed.

### Type-1 queue, wait and completion wrapper (`004fd060`)

Renamed to `QueueWaitAndCompleteType1FileOperation` after parent verification of Luna findings. Original EAX/EDX reach `QueueFileOperationType1ForRecordHandle`, with EBX forced0. It copies the resulting token into EDX; zero returns0. Otherwise it waits through `WaitForFileOperationToLeavePendingLocations`, ignores that scalar status, reloads the preserved token from EDX and calls `CompleteFileOperationAndReleaseRequest`, returning its scalar result. Explicitly restores EBX/ECX; plain RET, no stack inputs.

EDX carries the token through the verified preserving wait/completion helpers, not a second64-bit result. Type1 completion uses close result. No timeout, wait-status branch or independent readiness check; worker failure and ownership ordering remain unresolved. Ghidra annotation saved; no runtime I/O or executable modification.

### Waiting for file-operation pending locations (`004fc780`)

Renamed to `WaitForFileOperationToLeavePendingLocations` after complete wrapper assembly and existing helper-contract review. EAX identifier selects group `(id&31)*0x68`; all non-EAX registers preserved, plain RET, scalar EAX. Identifier0 or initially inactive group returns-3. Otherwise optional group+0x1c locking surrounds `FindFileOperationAndClassifyLocation`. It ANDs classification(-1 current,1 first queue,0 second/absent) with boolean node existence, so only found pending/current records keep waiting.

On the initialization thread (`CheckCurrentThreadIdentity(0)`), it services periodic callbacks with context0 and sleeps alertably with argument1; other threads wait on group event+0x5c. It loops until the filtered classification is zero, then returns `GetFileOperationPendingOrStoredStatus`. No timeout/cancellation or guarantee of successful I/O. Lock activation stability, event lifecycle and completion ordering remain unresolved; matching limits are saved in Ghidra. No runtime work occurred.

Sets+0x60=1,+0x64=255.

Publishes index `009f4f64` and calls `CreateLibraryManagedThread` with callback `004fbda0`, stack size0, priority1 and descriptor slot+4. ### Archived FCE and primary TGA loading (`004b7a60`)

Renamed to `LoadArchivedFceModelAndPrimaryTga` after independent full assembly verification of Luna's review. Raw inputs are EAX=target object, EDX=asset stem, EBX=texture square extent, ECX=optional four-byte colour input, and one stack DWORD=BIG archive base. The function preserves ESI/EDI/EBP, uses `RET 4`, and returns the allocated FCE block in EAX. The generated fastcall prototype omits meaningful inputs.

The loader formats `%s.fce`, resolves its archive offset/length, allocates and copies that entry, and invokes `BuildFceTriangleRenderRecords`. It then formats **`%s00.tga`**, not `%s.tga`, and borrows that entry directly from the archive. Optional colour bytes are zero-extended into four local DWORDs and converted by unresolved `0049c880`; the first three result DWORDs are copied to target offsets `0x8a8/0x8ac/0x8b0`.

`UpdateSingleFceTextureFromTga` receives the FCE block, archive TGA pointer, original EBX extent, reuse token zero, optional converted request, upload flag 1 and copy destination zero. Local lookup/allocation status, stem length and resource bounds are not checked here; underlying abort policy remains separate. Converter semantics and full ownership are unresolved. Ghidra contains the matching contract and limitations.
